declarations.description:
Read-only key/value pairs for a detail page: the Descriptions of antd and the DescriptionList of Polaris. Each
`c2-description-item` child is one pair. The items flow into as many columns as fit, up to
`--c2-description-list__grid--columns`, each at least `--c2-description-list__grid--min-column-width` wide, so the
same markup is three columns on a wide page and one on a phone without a media query. An item spans the full row
with `--c2-description-item--grid-column: 1 / -1`.

Whether a label sits above its value or beside it is CSS too: `--c2-description-item__label--width` set to a
length puts the label beside the value, and the value still wraps under it when the item is narrower than the
label plus `--c2-description-item__value--min-width`. Set the item variables on the list and every item inherits them.

Items with several values (`c2-description-value` children) line up in columns; `value-labels` names those
columns in a header row and `label-heading` heads the label column. Style the row through `--c2-description-list__value-header--*`
(or the `value-header` part), or hide it with `--c2-description-list__value-header--display: none`. The header hides itself when the values stack,
and each value then shows its column name. A list with value columns lays its items out in a single column.

Items with several values also compare them, for a comparison matrix or the two versions of a record:
`highlight="max"` or `"min"` marks the best value of each item (an item's own `highlight` overrides the list's, so
a price can be `min` in a list of `max`), `highlight="different"` marks every value that differs from the first
column, and `differences-only` hides the items whose values are all equal. Each item whose values differ carries
the custom state `different` (`c2-description-item:state(different)`), and each highlighted value the state
`highlighted`. `selected-column` marks one value column, and `column-selectable` turns the column names into
toggle buttons that select it and fire `selection-change`.

`c2-description-group` children (imported from `@c2n/components/description-list/description-group`) are titled
sections of items, collapsible if wanted: a record's properties by topic, or the steps of a calculation closed by
`kind="subtotal"` items and a `kind="total"`. With an `editor` on its
items the list is a property inspector, each value editable in place (see `c2-description-item`); put an "Add
property" button in the `actions` slot.

The list is exposed as a `list` and every item as a `listitem` holding a `term` and its `definition`.

```html
<c2-description-list aria-label="Customer">
  <c2-description-item label="Name">Ada Lovelace</c2-description-item>
  <c2-description-item label="Email">ada@example.com</c2-description-item>
  <c2-description-item label="Plan">Business</c2-description-item>
</c2-description-list>
```

declarations.description:
One label and value pair of a `c2-description-list`. The label comes from the `label` attribute, or from the
`label` slot when it needs markup (an icon, a tooltip); the value is the item's content, which can be anything from
plain text to a badge, a link or an avatar. An item with no value shows `empty-text`, so a missing field reads as
"—" instead of an empty gap.

An item can hold several values, one `c2-description-value` each: the price of a feature in each plan, a metric
this month and last. They line up in equal columns across the items of the list, and the list's `value-labels`
names those columns. The layout adapts on its own: when the label and the columns no longer fit on one line the
columns move under the label, and when the columns themselves no longer fit (each narrower than
`--c2-description-item__value-column--min-width`) the values stack, each with its column name as a caption.

The item compares its values: while they are not all equal it carries the custom state `different`, which a page
can style (`c2-description-item:state(different)`), and the list's `differences-only` hides it while they are.
`highlight` picks the values to mark, overriding the list's.

`kind="subtotal"` or `"total"` makes the item a line of a calculation: a rule above it and a heavier weight, so a
breakdown (a fee, a tax, a pay stub) reads down to its result. Group the steps in `c2-description-group` sections.

An item with an `editor` is a property the reader can change, as a record's sidebar in a CRM: an edit button
beside the value (and a click on the value) swaps it for a field of that type, loaded the first time an item is
edited, so a read-only list never ships it. Enter or leaving the field commits and fires `edit` with the new value;
Escape cancels. The item does not change its own content: the page writes the new value, or ignores the event to
refuse it.

declarations.description:
A titled section of a `c2-description-list`: its `c2-description-item` children sit under a heading, across the
full width of the list and in the list's own columns. Sections are how a record's properties are grouped
("Contact", "Billing") and how a calculation breaks down into steps (earnings, deductions, taxes), each closed by a
`kind="subtotal"` item.

`collapsible` makes the heading a disclosure button that closes and opens the section; the items sit in a native
`<details>`, so the browser's find-in-page still finds a closed section's text and opens it. `collapsed` closes it,
and follows the reader.
